subject: Re: MAP - Technical Evaluation Plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>; Ava Lin <ava.lin@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call recap & MAP (technical eval) - Redwood x Acme

Hi John / Ava,

Great to connect today. Quick recap from our discovery and the technical evaluation milestone we agreed to include in the Mutual Action Plan (MAP):

1) Objective: Validate that Redwood meets Acme's latency and cost targets for customer-facing summarization workflows.

2) Success criteria (benchmarks):
   - 95th percentile end-to-end latency: <= 350ms for 512-token generation at p95 under target concurrency (see below).
   - Cost target: <= $0.006 per 1k tokens equivalent for production inference when using batching + KV cache.
   - Quality: ROUGE-L / human spot-checks, no regression vs current baseline (Acme model) on 10 core prompts; zero high-severity hallucinations in sample set.

3) Model shortlist for eval (initial):
   - open-llama-13b-q4
   - starcoder-7b (if codegen paths matter for annotations)
   - meta-llama-2-13b-chat (quantized variant)
   - fallback: gpt-3.5-turbo (hosted) for availability comparison

4) Testbed & responsibilities:
   - Acme: provide 10 canonical prompts + 3 sample docs per prompt, traffic pattern (QPS/concurrency target), and a sandbox account or secure S3 share for data. (Owner: John)
   - Redwood SE (Camila): set up benchmark harness, run latency/cost sweeps, and populate the attached latency_benchmark_template.pdf. (Owner: Camila)
   - Redwood Sales/CS (Marissa): coordinate procurement for Dedicated trial capacity if needed and sync on timeline. (Owner: Marissa)

5) Dependencies & potential blockers:
   - Data access & NDA for sample docs (Acme IT procurement)
   - If on-prem evaluation is required, we need lead time for Private deployment review (security/compliance).

6) Target milestone dates (draft):
   - MAP draft shared: today (attached).
   - Data + prompt set delivered by Acme: 2027-06-30
   - Benchmark setup & first run: 2027-07-05
   - Results review / decision meeting: 2027-07-09
   - Target close (decision to move to pilot/procure Dedicated): 2027-07-30

I attached the MAP draft and the latency template for Camila to populate with initial numbers. Next steps: John, please confirm the target concurrency (QPS) and whether we can get a secure S3 share for the sample docs by COB Tuesday (2027-06-29).

Thanks,
Marissa
---
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachment: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft)
Attachment: latency_benchmark_template.pdf
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Lin <ava.lin@acme.com>, Kelly Bryant <kelly.bryant@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & MAP (technical eval) - Redwood x Acme

Thanks Marissa, very helpful summary. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Target concurrency: we expect a 99th-percentile burst up to 25 concurrent inference requests, steady-state around 6 QPS. For the benchmark please run tests at 1, 6, 12, and 25 concurrent threads.
- We'll get you the 10 canonical prompts and sample docs. I need to check with procurement about the S3 share (should be OK; if not, I'll provide an Azure blob link).
- On quality: we'll prioritize summary fidelity and hallucination checks. Can Camila include a small human-eval checklist we can use?

Also, curious on the cost target, is the $0.006/1k tokens a realistic baseline for the quantized 13B models with batching? Please flag if we should expect higher in the pilot.

John
John Doe
Director of AI Engineering | Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0120
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & MAP (technical eval) - Redwood x Acme

Appreciate the quick responses, John, that's exactly the concurrency dimensions we need. 

Camila, can you confirm the benchmark matrix includes 1/6/12/25 concurrent threads + p50/p90/p95/p99 buckets and also add a short human-eval checklist for hallucination/faithfulness? Suggested checklist items attached in the latency template.

Rishi / Dev, looping you both for a quick read on the procurement angle: if Acme wants a Dedicated reserved pool for the pilot, what's a realistic short-term commit we can offer to keep cost efficient while staying flexible? Also flag any onboarding prerequisites for Private if they ask for on-prem tests.

John, regarding the cost target: the $0.006/1k is aggressive but feasible under these assumptions: 13B quantized model, efficient batching, and 30% KV cache hit rate for repeated prefixes. Camila will run a cost sweep and surface a likely per-1k-token number across the concurrency spectrum. We'll call out expected variance.

Next steps (updated):
- Acme to share prompts + sample docs: target 2027-06-30
- Redwood SE to run initial benchmark & populate results: target 2027-07-05
- Quick sync to review results: 2027-07-09 (30m)

Thanks all,
Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP - Technical eval plan (benchmark matrix + checklist)

Hey team, attaching the filled benchmark template (stubbed) and adding clarifications: 

- Benchmark matrix: will include 1/6/12/25 concurrency runs; p50/p90/p95/p99 latency buckets; throughput (tokens/sec); and cost-per-1k-token estimate based on observed GPU utilization and batching efficiency.
- Models I'll run first: open-llama-13b-q4, meta-llama-2-13b-chat-quant, and a 7B fallback. I'll include results for the hosted fallback (gpt-3.5-turbo) purely for availability/quality comparison.
- Human-eval checklist (short):
   1) Does the summary accurately reflect the source document's key facts? (Yes/No)
   2) Any hallucinated facts? (List if Yes)
   3) Fluency score (1-5)
   4) Any PII leakage observed? (Yes/No)

Blockers: if we can't get data access by 2027-06-30, we'll push the first run out by a week. Also, if Acme requires on-prem execution for the benchmark, please confirm today, that adds ~2 weeks for infra prep and security onboarding.

I'll start baseline runs on Monday once we have the prompt set.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
